summary.text: Tim Moore is the Republican U.S. representative for North Carolina's 14th Congressional District and lost re-election on November 3, 2026 to Lakesha Womack; his term ends January 3, 2027.
A Kings Mountain attorney, he served in the North Carolina House of Representatives from 2002 to 2025, including ten years as Speaker, before winning election to Congress in 2024.

paragraphs.text: According to his official biography, Tim Moore is a lifelong resident of Kings Mountain, North Carolina, in Cleveland County.
He earned a bachelor's degree in political science from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill in 1992 and a law degree from Oklahoma City University School of Law in 1995.
After passing the North Carolina bar exam, he returned to Cleveland County, where his official biography says he has practiced law throughout his career.
Moore won election to the North Carolina House of Representatives in 2002 and served until 2025, representing District 111.
He was Speaker of the chamber from 2015 to 2025, and his official biography describes his priorities as Speaker as infrastructure development, education reform, and job creation.
In 2024 he won the general election for North Carolina's 14th Congressional District with 58.1% of the vote over Democrat Pamela Genant, succeeding Rep. Jeff Jackson, and took office January 3, 2025.
Moore serves on the House Committee on Financial Services (as Vice Chair) and the House Committee on the Budget for the 2025-2026 Congress.
He won the March 3, 2026 Republican primary with 83.0% of the vote over Kate Barr.
His official biography says he lives in Kings Mountain and is the father of two sons, McRae and Wilson.
He received 48.9% of the vote to Lakesha Womack's 51.1%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
